title: BalanceDef

currency_name.description: Display name of the currency (engine id currency), as the client shows it. Cosmetic: no code reads it as logic.

base_exp_table_id.description: EXP table (exp.*) for base levels. Its length sets the max base level (Exp).

stat_points_per_base_level.description: Stat points awarded on reaching a base level. Variable: base_level (the level just reached).

skill_points_per_job_level.description: Skill points awarded on reaching a job level. Variable: job_level (the level just reached).

starting_stat_points.description: Stat points a new character starts with.

starting_stat_value.description: Value every primary stat starts at.

max_stat_value.description: Highest value a primary stat can be raised to (by points, before equipment and buffs).

stat_point_cost.description: Stat points needed to raise a stat by one. Variable: stat_value (the stat's current value, before the raise).

free_below_base_level.description: A character below this base level resets for free: the item is not used up (its cooldown still runs). 0 means never free.

refuse_in_combat.description: True to refuse a reset while the character dealt or took damage within regen.out_of_combat_delay_ms.

refuse_when_dead.description: True to refuse a reset while the character is dead.

reset.description: When a stat or skill reset (reset_stats, reset_skills) is free or refused (T-503).

progression.description: Stat point, skill point and level cap numbers.

min_damage.description: Lowest damage a hit that lands can deal.

max_damage.description: Highest damage a single hit can deal.

crit_multiplier.description: Damage multiplier on a critical hit, as a formula. Caster and t_ variables are allowed (e.g. 1.5 + luk * 0.005); a constant is fine.

player_attack_range.description: A player's auto-attack range in cells (Chebyshev) while unarmed. An equipped weapon uses its own attack_range instead.

player_repath_interval_ms.description: Shortest time between two path searches of a player walking into attack range of its target.

combat.description: Damage and chance clamps applied after the combat formulas.

max_path_length.description: Longest path, in cells (steps), a search may return; a longer route counts as "no path".

max_nodes_expanded.description: Most nodes a single search may expand before it gives up.

movement.description: Limits on path searches (grid movement, ARCHITECTURE §4).

bucket_size.description: Side of one AOI bucket, in cells.

view_radius.description: How many buckets around its own an observer sees (Chebyshev distance in buckets).

max_visible.description: Most entities one observer sees from its window, itself included: the nearest, plus those always visible (itself, its attack target, its attackers), which are never cut.

cap_hysteresis.description: Ranks an entity already shown may slip before it is cut. A new entity enters at rank max_visible - cap_hysteresis or better; one already shown stays until it ranks past max_visible (nearest first, then lowest id). From 0 to below max_visible.

cap_reserved_monsters.description: Slots of max_visible kept for the nearest monsters while there are that many. Slots a kind does not use go back to the others.

cap_reserved_npcs.description: Slots of max_visible kept for the nearest NPCs while there are that many.

cap_reserved_items.description: Slots of max_visible kept for the nearest ground items while there are that many; items the observer may pick up come first.

cap_reserved_margin.description: Ranks an entity already shown may slip past its kind's reservation, or past cap_pinned_chasers, and keep its slot. 0 or more. All three reservations together must leave at least one slot below the cutoff (max_visible - cap_hysteresis), for the observer itself.

cap_pinned_chasers.description: How many monsters chasing an observer, nearest first, are always visible to it before they have hit it. The others rank like any monster, so a long train cannot bypass the cap. 0 or more; with cap_reserved_margin, below max_visible.

aoi.description: Area of interest: which entities each observer is sent (ARCHITECTURE §3).

start_map_id.description: Map (map.*) a new character appears on.

start_x.description: Start cell X on that map's logic grid; the cell must be walkable.

start_y.description: Start cell Y on that map's logic grid; the cell must be walkable.

start_facing.description: Facing at the start, a Directions term (n, ne, ... nw).

start_job_id.description: Job (job.*) a new character starts in.

quantity.description: How many, at least 1. An equipment item becomes that many entries.

equipped.description: True to wear it from the start (equipment only; the usual equip rules for the start job apply).

items.description: One item a new character starts with.

start_items.description: What a new character carries (and wears) when it first joins. Ids are validated at load. Empty means nothing.

new_character.description: Where and as what a newly created character starts (the server's player join, T-205).

think_interval_ms.description: How often an awake aggressive monster looks for a player to attack.

wander_pause_min_ms.description: Shortest pause an idle monster waits before it wanders again.

wander_pause_max_ms.description: Longest pause an idle monster waits before it wanders again (picked uniformly between min and max).

wander_radius.description: How far from its home cell (Chebyshev, in cells) a wandering monster may walk.

repath_interval_ms.description: Shortest time between two path searches of a chasing or returning monster.

return_timeout_ms.description: A returning monster that is not home after this long is put back on its home cell.

heal_on_return.description: A monster that gave up a chase and arrives home is healed to full HP when true (the damage-share table resets either way). Defaults to true: otherwise a monster could be worn down by hit-and-run.

ai.description: Monster behavior timings shared by every monster (ARCHITECTURE §6.6); per-monster ranges are in MonsterAiDef.

respawn_hp_percent.description: Share of max_hp a player respawns with, in percent (1–100). Rounded down, at least 1 HP.

exp_penalty_percent.description: Base EXP lost on death, in percent of the current base level's requirement (0 = no penalty). Rounded down; never takes EXP below 0, so a character never loses a level. Nothing is lost at the max level, where EXP is always 0.

corpse_ms.description: How long a dead monster stays in the world (Dead, not targetable) before it is despawned, so clients can play its death animation. Simulated milliseconds from the tick it died in; 0 despawns it on the next tick. The monster's respawn timer counts from the death, not from the despawn.

death.description: What happens when a player dies and respawns (the server's combat loop).

priority_ms.description: How long after the drop only the top damager may pick an item up; after that anyone may.

lifetime_ms.description: How long a ground item stays before it disappears.

spread_radius.description: Drops land on a random walkable cell within this many cells of the death cell (0 = always the death cell). Never on a blocked cell.

loot.description: Ground items a monster drops: where they land, who may take them and how long they stay.

out_of_combat_delay_ms.description: An entity that deals or takes damage does not regenerate for this many simulated milliseconds afterwards (and the dead never do).

max_entries.description: Most entries a character can hold (a stack counts once, each equipment item once, worn ones included).

burdened_percent.description: At or above this share of the weight limit natural HP and SP regeneration stops (burdened). 1–100.

overweight_percent.description: At or above this share the character also cannot attack (overweight). From burdened_percent to 100.

pickup_range.description: A player picks up a ground item within this many cells (Chebyshev) of it, walking there first. 0 or more.

dropped_lifetime_ms.description: How long an item a player dropped stays on the ground, in simulated milliseconds. Above 0.

two_handed_weapon_types.description: Weapon types held in both hands (WeaponTypes terms): such a weapon in weapon also takes the shield slot, so equipping it takes a shield off, and equipping a shield takes it off.

inventory.description: A character's inventory: entry count, weight thresholds, pick-up range, dropped items and two-handed weapons (ARCHITECTURE §6.8).

talk_range.description: How close (Chebyshev, in cells) a player must be to start or keep a dialogue with an NPC. A talk from farther walks the player in first; walking farther than this from the NPC ends the dialogue and any service it opened. At least 1.

refine_needs_service.description: When true the refine intent works only while an NPC's refine service is open (an open_service action) and in reach.

dialogue.description: Talking to NPCs and the services they open (T-601, ARCHITECTURE §6.4).

description: The root of content/balance.yaml: tuning numbers and small formulas that are not per-entity stats (ARCHITECTURE §6.5). A single set per game, so it has no id. Progression and combat code reads its numbers from here instead of hardcoding them.
